_meta.title: Finish-off build briefs for Jamie Wigg's apps
_meta.purpose: Paste-ready 'Create an iOS app that…' prompts for Lovable / Blink / v0 / Bolt. Each brief was generated from the actual app source in this repo.

apps.name: Heartbeat
apps.oneLiner: An AI friend who listens, 24/7 and judgment-free
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that is a warm, always-available AI companion called Heartbeat — an emotional-support friend you can talk to any time, free and judgment-free. Open with a multi-step onboarding flow: a welcome screen, a personality picker (Listener with empathy-first, Advisor for practical help, Entertainer to keep things light, Mentor for wise guidance), a language selector, and a voice picker (Maya warm, James calm, Sofia caring, or Text-only). The main screen is a full-screen chat conversation with a gradient circular avatar in the header, animated incoming-message typing dots, and slide-in message bubbles. Include a text input plus a microphone button that records the user's voice using native iOS speech-to-text, and read the AI's replies aloud with native text-to-speech in the chosen voice. Powered by an AI chat model (Claude) that adapts its tone to the selected personality and language. A slide-out settings panel lets the user change personality, voice, and language on the fly, and a danger-zone button clears all data. Store the user's chosen personality, voice, language, and full conversation history locally on-device — nothing leaves the phone. Visual style: modern dark theme, deep slate navy background (#0F172A) with a vivid pink-to-magenta accent (#FF6B9D), rounded chat bubbles, soft pulse animations, and a friendly, comforting feel. Smooth, native iOS transitions throughout.

apps.name: BookReader Pro
apps.oneLiner: Scan any page and read it aloud together
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app called BookReader Pro that helps dyslexic and struggling readers by scanning printed pages and reading them aloud. Use a swipeable five-screen carousel with a bottom page-dot indicator and a reading-streak counter in the header. Home shows a friendly reading-buddy avatar and cards linking to each feature. Scan screen: use the native iOS camera to photograph any book page, run on-device OCR to extract the text, and show a progress bar while it reads the page. Reader screen displays the extracted text in a large, comfortable font and reads it aloud with native text-to-speech, highlighting each word in sync as it is spoken, with play/stop controls and adjustable speed (Slow, Calm, Quick). A Library stores every scanned page (title + date) so users can reopen and re-read them. A Reading Buddy chat tab uses an AI model (Claude) to explain hard words, summarize the page, or answer questions in warm, simple, encouraging language, with quick-tap suggestion chips. Settings: the user's name, an on-device Claude API key field, a read-aloud toggle, voice speed, a dyslexia-friendly OpenDyslexic font toggle, a bigger-text toggle, and a Fast/Smart model choice. Store everything (books, streak, preferences, key) locally on-device. Visual style: dark violet-and-pink gradient theme (#a78bfa/#f472b6), rounded cards, spring animations, Lexend reading font, gentle and confidence-building.

apps.name: FitCoach Pro
apps.oneLiner: AI form-check coach and personalized workout plans
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app called FitCoach Pro, a personal AI fitness coach with real-time form feedback. Use a swipeable five-screen carousel with a bottom page-dot indicator and a workout-streak counter in the header, plus a motivating coach avatar on Home. Form Check screen: let the user record or upload an exercise video or photo using the native iOS camera and photo library, show an analyzing progress bar, then use an AI vision model (Claude) to return specific coaching feedback on their form and technique. Workout Plan screen: the user types an exercise (e.g. bench press, squats, pull-ups) and the AI generates a customized 10-rep plan, presented as exercise cards with a large built-in rep/rest timer and a progress bar. Progress screen: log completed workouts and show weekly charts and strength milestones. Settings: the user's name, an on-device Claude API key field, a fitness-level picker (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced), a voice-feedback toggle, and voice speed — with coaching cues spoken aloud through native text-to-speech. Store the API key, fitness level, workout logs, streak, and preferences locally on-device; nothing is uploaded to a server. Visual style: bold, athletic dark theme with a fiery red-to-orange gradient (#ef4444/#f97316) and green accents for actions, rounded cards, spring animations, monospace timer digits, and an energetic, motivating tone throughout. Smooth native iOS transitions.

apps.name: MathTutor Pro
apps.oneLiner: Patient AI math tutor that rebuilds confidence
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app called MathTutor Pro, a warm and patient AI maths tutor designed especially for learners who are dyslexic, have ADHD, or have lost confidence in maths. Use a swipeable five-screen carousel with a bottom page-dot indicator, a learning-streak counter in the header, and a friendly tutor avatar on Home. Solve screen offers three ways in: type a problem, photograph it with the native iOS camera (OCR the handwriting/print), or say it out loud via native speech-to-text — then the AI (Claude) works through it step by step in plain, encouraging language, never rushing. Tutor screen is a chat where the learner can talk through any concept and get calm, step-by-step explanations with quick-tap suggestion chips. Practice screen generates fresh problems matched to the learner's level, with an answer field and supportive feedback. Settings: the user's name, an on-device Claude API key field, a read-aloud voice toggle and speed, and a dyslexia-friendly reading font. Read explanations aloud with native text-to-speech. Store the name, key, streak, and preferences locally on-device — everything stays private on the phone. Visual style: calming dark theme with an emerald-green-to-teal gradient (#10b981/#06b6d4) plus violet and amber accents, rounded cards, gentle spring animations, Lexend font, and a reassuring, confidence-building tone. Smooth native iOS transitions throughout.

apps.name: StudyMate
apps.oneLiner: AI study plans, quizzes, and auto-flashcards
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app called StudyMate, an AI study companion that builds personalized study plans, generates quizzes, and creates flashcards. Use a swipeable five-screen carousel with a bottom page-dot indicator, a study-streak counter in the header, and a focused study-buddy avatar on Home. Study Plan screen: the user enters their subjects and topics (e.g. Biology cells/photosynthesis, Math algebra/fractions) and the AI (Claude) produces a personalized daily study schedule tailored to them. Quiz screen: the user names a topic and the AI generates practice questions, accepts typed answers, and grades the work with helpful explanations. Flashcards screen: the AI auto-generates a flashcard deck for any topic, presented as tappable flip cards with spaced-repetition review built in. Settings: the user's name, learning goals, subjects, an on-device Claude API key field, and a read-aloud voice toggle and speed, with content spoken via native iOS text-to-speech. Store the study plans, generated quizzes, flashcard decks, streak, goals, and API key locally on-device — nothing is sent to a server. Visual style: sleek dark theme with a purple primary and green accents, rounded cards, spring animations, Lexend/Inter typography, and a smart, motivating, focused feel. Smooth native iOS carousel swiping and transitions throughout, optimized for phone screens.

apps.name: SpellingBuddy
apps.oneLiner: Judgment-free writing coach for confident spelling
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app called SpellingBuddy, a warm, judgment-free writing coach that helps dyslexic and less-confident writers with spelling, grammar, and clarity. Use a swipeable five-screen carousel with a bottom page-dot indicator and a friendly writing-coach avatar on Home. Write screen: a large free-typing text area where, as the user types, the AI (Claude) gives real-time, gentle spelling and grammar suggestions and rewrites, in plain supportive language rather than red-pen corrections. Explain screen: the user types (or taps) any word or phrase and the AI explains what it means simply and clearly. History screen: every writing sample the user creates is saved so they can revisit and learn from it. Settings: the user's name, an on-device Claude API key field, a dyslexia-friendly font toggle, a text-size control, a speak-aloud toggle, and voice speed — with suggestions and explanations read aloud using native iOS text-to-speech. Store all writing samples, the API key, and preferences locally on-device; nothing leaves the phone. Visual style: encouraging dark theme with soft purple accents, rounded cards, spring animations, a comfortable reading font, and a calm, confidence-building tone that never makes the writer feel judged. Smooth native iOS carousel transitions and a mobile-first layout throughout.

apps.name: LanguageLens
apps.oneLiner: Learn languages naturally by speaking and listening
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app called LanguageLens that teaches languages the natural way — through pronunciation, real conversation, and vocabulary building. Use a swipeable five-screen carousel with a bottom page-dot indicator and an enthusiastic language-partner avatar on Home. Pronunciation screen: the user types any word or phrase and hears it pronounced perfectly using native iOS text-to-speech, shown on a word card with a phonetic breakdown. Conversation screen: a chat with an AI language partner (Claude) that talks naturally in the target language, adapts to the learner's level, and offers quick-start topic chips (simple greeting, tell a story, learning tips); the AI's replies are read aloud with native text-to-speech. Vocabulary screen: a personal word bank that automatically collects new words from the user's conversations, ready to review and practice. Settings: the user's name, an on-device Claude API key field, a language picker (Spanish, French, German), a voice toggle, and voice speed. Store the vocabulary bank, chat history, chosen language, API key, and preferences locally on-device — everything stays private on the phone. Visual style: inviting dark theme with warm gradient accents, rounded cards, spring animations, clean Inter/Lexend typography, flag emojis for languages, and an encouraging, immersive feel. Smooth native iOS carousel swiping and transitions, mobile-first throughout.

apps.name: MeetingMind
apps.oneLiner: Turn meetings into decisions and tracked action items
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that turns meetings into summaries, decisions, and tracked action items, presented as five swipeable screens with a page-dot indicator and a daily-streak badge in the header. Screen 1 is a Home hub with a time-aware greeting and cards linking to each feature. Screen 2, Record, uses the device microphone and native on-device speech-to-text to live-transcribe a meeting, then an 'Analyze meeting' button. Screen 3, Analyze, lets the user paste a transcript or notes. Both feed Claude with a system prompt that extracts key decisions, action items with owners, and discussion points, streaming the result back. Screen 4, Action Items, shows all extracted and manually-added tasks with a tap-to-complete checkbox and date, persisted on device. Screen 5, Settings, stores the user's name, their own Claude API key, an optional ElevenLabs key, a voice-summaries toggle, voice-speed pills (Slow/Normal/Fast), and an AI-model choice (Fast/Smart). Analyzed summaries can be read aloud using ElevenLabs text-to-speech or native iOS speech synthesis. Everything stays in on-device storage with nothing sent to any server except the AI APIs the user configures. Visual style: a polished dark UI on a deep navy-slate background with sky-blue accents, soft glassy cards with rounded corners, subtle spring animations, a floating pill navigation bar, and Inter typography. Include a daily streak counter that increments when the user analyzes a meeting or adds an action.

apps.name: SmartGrocery
apps.oneLiner: Scan receipts, find cheaper alternatives and coupons
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that helps people save money on groceries, built as five swipeable screens with a page-dot indicator and a 'money saved' badge in the header. Screen 1 is a Home hub with a time-aware greeting and feature cards. Screen 2, Scan Receipt, opens the camera or photo library and runs on-device OCR (native Vision text recognition) to read the receipt's items and prices, showing a live progress bar. Screen 3, Price Suggestions, is a chat where the user asks about any product and Claude returns cheaper alternatives and practical cost-saving tips, with dollar amounts highlighted. Screen 4, Find Coupons, takes a list of grocery items and asks Claude to return available coupons per item with store and savings amount, then displays coupon cards and a big 'Potential Savings' total. Screen 5, Settings, stores the user's name, their own Claude API key, an optional ElevenLabs key, a voice-suggestions toggle, and voice-speed pills. AI grocery tips and coupon totals can be read aloud with ElevenLabs text-to-speech or native iOS speech synthesis. All data lives in on-device storage; nothing is uploaded except calls to the AI services the user configures. Visual style: a rich dark UI on a deep forest-green background with emerald and gold accents, glassy rounded cards, gold coupon and savings callouts, smooth spring animations, a floating pill nav bar, and Inter typography. Include a streak that grows each day the user scans a receipt or finds coupons.

apps.name: NutriAI
apps.oneLiner: Snap meals, track macros, get AI meal plans
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that tracks nutrition and coaches healthier eating, built as five swipeable screens with a page-dot indicator, a friendly nutrition-coach avatar, and a daily-streak badge. Screen 1 is a Home hub with a time-aware greeting and the coach introduction. Screen 2, Scan a Meal, opens the camera to photograph food and uses AI vision to identify the dish and break it into calories, protein, carbs, and fat as macro cards, with an 'Add to diary' button. Screen 3, Food Diary, is a per-day log showing total and remaining calories against the user's goal with a progress bar, per-macro totals, a timestamped entry list, manual food entry, and a clear-day option. Screen 4, Meal Plans, takes a dietary goal and asks Claude to generate a personalized weekly plan honoring the user's calorie target and restrictions, streamed back. Screen 5, Settings, stores name, the user's own Claude API key, dietary restrictions/allergies, daily calorie goal, voice-speed pills, and an AI-model choice (Fast/Smart). Coach responses can be read aloud with native iOS speech synthesis. All data stays in on-device storage; only the configured Claude API is called externally. Visual style: a warm dark UI on a deep green background with lime and magenta accents, glassy rounded cards, macro stat tiles, gradient progress bars, spring animations, a floating pill nav bar, and Inter/Lexend typography. Include a streak that increments each day the user scans, logs, or plans a meal.

apps.name: CodeMentor
apps.oneLiner: Warm AI code review, debugging, and learning
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that is a warm, encouraging AI code mentor, built as five swipeable screens with a page-dot indicator, a mentor avatar, and a daily-streak badge. Screen 1 is a Home hub with a time-aware greeting and feature cards. Screen 2, Review, takes pasted code in a monospaced editor and sends it to Claude with a kind, confidence-building system prompt that spots bugs, security issues, inefficiencies, and missing edge cases while explaining the 'why'; responses stream in live and each review is saved. Screen 3, Debug, takes an error message plus code and returns a root-cause diagnosis and fix. Screen 4, Learn, is a multi-turn chat about any coding question with conversation history. Screen 5, Saved Reviews, lists stored reviews (kept up to 30) as tappable cards that expand to show the original code and feedback. A Settings modal stores the user's name, their own Claude API key, a read-aloud voice toggle with speed pills, a dyslexia-friendly font toggle (OpenDyslexic with wider spacing and line height), and an AI-model choice (Haiku/Opus). Feedback can be spoken aloud using native iOS speech synthesis. All data stays in on-device storage; only the configured Claude API is called. Visual style: a developer-dark UI on a near-black navy background with slate and red accents, glassy rounded cards, JetBrains Mono code blocks, left-border 'step' cards, spring animations, and a floating pill nav bar. Include a streak that increments each day the user reviews, debugs, or chats.

apps.name: StoryStudio
apps.oneLiner: Turn ideas into short-form video scripts fast
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that turns story ideas into short-form (30–60 second) video scripts, built as five swipeable screens with a page-dot indicator, an energetic creative-partner avatar, and a 'scripts written' badge. Screen 1 is a Home hub with a time-aware greeting and feature cards. Screen 2, Write Script, takes a described idea and asks Claude with a cinematic screenwriting system prompt to produce a visual script with scene descriptions, camera cues, and pacing markers, streamed live into a styled script box. Screen 3, Edit Pacing, takes the script and returns 3–4 specific suggestions to improve timing, transitions, hooks, and emotional beats. Screen 4, Auto Captions, splits the script into timed caption rows with adjustable font size (Small/Normal/Large). Screen 5, Export Ready, shows the polished script, suggests mood-matched background music tracks, and offers a copy-to-clipboard button. A Settings screen stores the user's name, their own Claude API key, a read-scripts-aloud voice toggle with speed pills, a dyslexia-friendly font toggle (OpenDyslexic), and an AI-model choice (Fast/Smart); scripts can be read aloud with native iOS speech synthesis. All data stays in on-device storage; only the configured Claude API is called. Visual style: a cinematic dark UI on a near-black background with pink/rose and gold accents, glassy rounded cards, gradient buttons, spring animations, an animated avatar, a floating pill nav bar, and Inter/Lexend typography. Include a streak that grows each time the user generates a script.

apps.name: VoiceJournal
apps.oneLiner: Speak your feelings; get compassionate AI reflection
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that is a compassionate voice-first wellness journal, built as five swipeable screens with a page-dot indicator, a gentle wellness-coach avatar, and a daily-streak badge. Screen 1 is a Home hub with a time-aware greeting and the coach introduction. Screen 2, Record Thoughts, has a pulsing microphone button that uses native on-device speech-to-text to transcribe the user speaking freely, then sends the transcript to Claude with a warm, non-clinical wellness system prompt that reflects feelings and asks a gentle follow-up question, streamed as chat bubbles. Screen 3, Check Mood, offers an eight-emoji mood grid (calm, peaceful, sad, anxious, frustrated, grateful, confused, energized) plus a chat where the user explains what happened and gets perspective shifts. Screen 4, Insights, shows saved journal entries, most-common mood, total entries, and recent-entry cards. Screen 5, Wellness, generates a short tailored 5–10 minute grounding or coping practice based on recent moods. Settings stores name, the user's own Claude API key, a read-aloud voice toggle with speed pills, a dyslexia-friendly font toggle (OpenDyslexic), and an AI-model choice (Fast/Insightful); replies can be spoken with native iOS speech synthesis. All data stays private in on-device storage; only the configured Claude API is called. Visual style: a soothing dark UI on a deep purple background with lavender and mint accents, glassy rounded cards, breathing avatar animation, mood tiles, a floating pill nav bar, and Inter/Lexend typography. Include a streak that increments each day the user records, logs a mood, or requests a practice.

apps.name: LifeAudit
apps.oneLiner: One assessment mapping your whole-life health picture
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that is a holistic whole-person health self-assessment completed in about five minutes, presented as a single scrolling questionnaire with a top progress bar that fills as answers are given. Organize questions into six emoji-headed sections: Physical Health (sleep, daytime energy, and stress sliders, weekly-exercise radio options, and an optional chronic-conditions text field), Mental & Emotional Health (stress, anxiety, and mood sliders plus coping-strategy checkboxes), Relationships & Connection (connection and relationship-satisfaction sliders plus closest-relationship checkboxes), Work & Purpose (employment-status radios plus work-stress and sense-of-purpose sliders), Basic Needs & Safety (financial-security slider plus food-security, housing, and personal-safety radios), and Values & Meaning (what-gives-life-meaning checkboxes and an optional free-text notes field). A 'Generate My Report' button computes an overall health score out of 100 from the weighted answers and switches to a report view showing the score with an interpretation, key insights, red-flag 'areas needing support' (e.g. burnout risk, isolation, severe anxiety, sleep deprivation), and recommended companion wellness apps with reasons, followed by a next-steps list and a crisis-helpline warning. Include Clear, Back-to-assessment, and Retake buttons. All scoring runs entirely on-device with no network calls or accounts — fully offline and private. Visual style: a calm dark UI on a slate-navy gradient with emerald-green accents, rounded cards with a green left border, custom green slider thumbs, a gradient recommendations panel, and clean system typography, fully responsive for phone screens.

apps.name: FOCUS
apps.oneLiner: Deep-work timer built for ADHD brains
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that is a deep-work focus timer designed for ADHD and easily-distracted minds, called FOCUS. Build four bottom tabs: Timer, Sounds, Stats, and Settings. The Timer tab centers on a large animated circular progress ring with three switchable modes (Focus, Short Break, Long Break), a task field labeled 'What are you working on?', and start/pause/reset controls plus an adaptive Pomodoro that nudges session length based on completions. Include an optional body-doubling presence mode. The Sounds tab is an ambient mixer with looping options — Brown Noise, Rain, Café, 40Hz Gamma binaural, White Noise, and Lo-Fi Synth — each with individual volume, mixable and playing in the background with the screen locked. The Stats tab shows daily focused-minutes, streaks, session history, and a weekly bar chart. Settings covers durations, haptics, notifications, and appearance. Store all sessions, sound presets, and stats on-device with no account or server. Visual style: dark near-black background (#07070f) with violet accents (#7c3aed), frosted glass cards, Space Grotesk headings, Inter body, soft glow shadows, subtle particle celebration on completion. Free tier allows 3 focus sessions per day; a paywall unlocks unlimited sessions, all ambient sounds, and full stats via a $4.99/month auto-renewing subscription with a short free trial, implemented with StoreKit 2 and a restore-purchases option.

apps.name: DRIFT
apps.oneLiner: AI sleep coach for better nights
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that is an AI-powered sleep coach called DRIFT with the tagline 'Sleep smarter. Wake better.' Build four bottom tabs: Tonight, Log, Trends, and Coach. The Tonight tab shows tonight's recommended bedtime and wake time with hour/minute wheel pickers, a current Sleep Score ring, a Sleep Debt indicator, and a calming free wind-down session with ambient audio. The Log tab lets the user record last night's sleep — bedtime, wake time, duration, quality, and notes. The Trends tab visualizes consistency, average duration, sleep-debt accumulation, and bedtime drift over weeks with charts. The Coach tab delivers personalized AI insights, smart debt-payoff schedules, and adaptive bedtime recommendations generated from the user's logged data. Store all sleep logs, schedules, and preferences on-device with no account required. Visual style: deep indigo-black background (#04040f) with slowly drifting blurred ambient orbs in indigo (#4f46e5) and periwinkle (#818cf8), frosted glass panels, Space Grotesk display type, Inter body, and a soft nighttime glow throughout. Offer a 7-day free trial, then gate the full Coach behind a $5.99/month auto-renewing subscription implemented with StoreKit 2, with clear 'no charge today' trial messaging, cancel-anytime copy, and restore purchases.

apps.name: PULSE
apps.oneLiner: Simple habit tracker with streaks
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that is a clean habit tracker called PULSE. Build four bottom tabs: Today, Habits, Stats, and Settings. The Today tab lists the day's habits as tappable cards the user checks off, with satisfying haptics and an animated ring showing today's completion percentage. The Habits tab manages the habit list — add a habit with a name (placeholder 'e.g. Morning run'), an icon, a color, and a frequency (daily or specific weekdays), with edit, reorder, and archive. The Stats tab shows per-habit current and best streaks, a GitHub-style completion heatmap calendar, and weekly/monthly consistency percentages. Settings covers daily reminder notifications, appearance, and data. Persist all habits, check-ins, and streaks on-device using local storage with no account or server. Visual style: dark background with vivid accent gradients, frosted glass cards, rounded corners, Space Grotesk headings and Inter body, smooth spring animations on check-off. The free plan is capped at 3 habits with an inline 'Free plan: 3 habits max' banner; a paywall unlocks unlimited habits, the full heatmap, and reminders via a $3.99/month auto-renewing subscription implemented with StoreKit 2, including restore purchases and a clear upgrade sheet.

apps.name: TRIM
apps.oneLiner: Track and tame your subscriptions
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that is a subscription tracker called TRIM that helps people see and cut recurring spending. Build four bottom tabs: Dashboard, Add, Insights, and Settings. The Dashboard shows total monthly and yearly spend at a glance, a list of active subscriptions with logo/color, price, billing cycle, and next renewal date, sorted by upcoming renewal, with an 'almost renewing' highlight. The Add tab is a form to create a subscription — name (placeholder 'e.g. Netflix, Spotify…'), cost, billing cycle (monthly, yearly, weekly, custom), first billing date, category, and color. The Insights tab breaks spending down by category, projects annual cost, flags the priciest and least-used subscriptions, and estimates potential savings. Settings covers renewal-reminder notifications, currency, and data export. Store all subscriptions and settings on-device with no account or server, and schedule local notifications a few days before each renewal. Visual style: dark background, frosted glass cards, bold totals in Space Grotesk, Inter body, colorful category accents, and smooth transitions. Offer a limited free tier, then a one-time paywall that unlocks unlimited subscriptions, full insights, and renewal reminders for a single $3.99 in-app purchase (non-consumable) implemented with StoreKit 2, with restore purchases — 'unlock once, yours forever.'

apps.name: SCAN
apps.oneLiner: Snap receipts, track expenses, export for tax
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that is a receipt and expense tracker called SCAN, aimed at freelancers and sole traders. Build four bottom tabs: Scan, Expenses, Reports, and Settings. The Scan tab captures a receipt via the camera or photo library, runs on-device text recognition (VisionKit) to auto-extract merchant, date, total, and tax, then presents an editable form with fields for merchant (placeholder 'e.g. Bunnings'), amount, category, GST/tax, and a note (placeholder 'Client name, project, etc.'), saving the cropped receipt image. The Expenses tab is a searchable, filterable list of saved receipts grouped by month with running totals and thumbnail previews. The Reports tab summarizes spend by category and period, computes total GST, and exports a CSV for tax/accounting. Settings covers currency (default AUD), categories, and data export or clear. Store all receipts, images, and data on-device with no account or cloud upload. Visual style: dark background, frosted glass cards, crisp Space Grotesk figures, Inter body, category color chips, and a clean scan-preview UI. The free plan allows 10 receipts; a one-time paywall unlocks unlimited receipts, reports, and CSV export for a single $4.99 non-consumable in-app purchase via StoreKit 2 — 'upgrade once, yours forever' — with restore purchases.

apps.name: GLOW
apps.oneLiner: Your daily skincare routine and skin journal
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that is a skincare tracker called GLOW. Build four bottom tabs: Routine, Scan, Journal, and Products. The Routine tab shows editable AM and PM step-by-step routines built from the user's products, with check-off, haptics, and daily completion tracking. The Scan tab is an ingredient analyzer: the user pastes or types a product's ingredient list (placeholder 'e.g. CeraVe Moisturising Cream') and taps Analyse to flag notable, comedogenic, or irritating ingredients and give a plain-language summary. The Journal tab is a daily skin log where the user records how their skin feels with a mood selector (Great, Good, OK, Bad, Ugh), notes, and an optional photo, building a visual timeline of skin over time. The Products tab is a shelf of saved products with brand, name, type, and notes, plus add/edit. Store all routines, products, journal entries, and photos on-device with no account or server. Visual style: soft dark aesthetic with warm glowing accents, frosted glass cards, rounded corners, Space Grotesk headings, Inter body, gentle animations. The free plan caps the shelf at 5 products; a one-time paywall unlocks unlimited products, full ingredient analysis, and the complete skin journal for a single $3.99 non-consumable in-app purchase via StoreKit 2, with restore purchases.

apps.name: MACRO
apps.oneLiner: Fast calorie and macro tracking with goals
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that is a calorie and macro counter called MACRO. Build four bottom tabs: Today, Log, Trends, and Goals. The Today tab shows a calories ring plus protein, carbs, and fat progress bars against daily goals, remaining kcal, water intake in glasses, and a logging streak. The Log tab lets the user add meals fast — a searchable built-in database of 50+ common foods (placeholder 'Search 50+ foods…') plus custom entries with calories, protein, carbs, and fat, organized by meal (breakfast, lunch, dinner, snacks) with per-meal and daily totals. The Trends tab charts calories and macros over time, weight logged in kg, and adherence. The Goals tab sets calorie and macro targets with adjustable sliders, a water goal, and a weight goal. Store all foods, logs, weight, and goals on-device with no account or server. Visual style: dark background, frosted glass cards, bold Space Grotesk numerals, Inter body, vivid macro-colored rings and bars, smooth animations. Offer a short free trial, then a lifetime paywall unlocking unlimited logging, full trends, and custom goals for a single $4.99 non-consumable in-app purchase ('Unlock Lifetime') via StoreKit 2, with restore purchases and clear trial-ended messaging.

apps.name: LAPSE
apps.oneLiner: One photo a day, a year in a grid
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that is a daily photo journal called LAPSE, built around capturing one photo a day. Build four bottom tabs: Today, Timeline, Calendar, and Settings. The Today tab prompts the user to add today's moment — take or pick a photo, add an optional caption (placeholder 'Add a moment caption… (optional)'), and save it, showing whether today is already captured and the current daily streak. The Timeline tab is a scrollable grid of all daily photos, newest first, tappable to open a full-screen viewer with caption and date and swipe navigation. The Calendar tab is a month view with photo thumbnails on captured days and empty markers on missed days, so the user can browse and backfill by date. Settings covers a daily reminder notification time, appearance, and data export. Store all photos, captions, and streak data on-device with no account or cloud upload. Visual style: dark, photo-forward aesthetic where images are the hero, minimal chrome, frosted glass overlays, Space Grotesk headings, Inter body, smooth transitions, and a subtle streak flourish. Offer a limited free number of days, then a one-time paywall unlocking unlimited photo history and reminders for a single $2.99 non-consumable in-app purchase via StoreKit 2, with restore purchases and a clean unlock sheet.

apps.name: HYPE
apps.oneLiner: Daily affirmations that build real momentum
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that is a daily affirmations app called HYPE with the spirit 'Lifetime hype.' Build three bottom tabs: Today, Saved, and Settings. On first launch, ask for the user's first name to personalize affirmations. The Today tab presents a large, beautifully typeset daily affirmation card the user can swipe through, favorite (heart), and share as an image, with a build-a-streak counter for daily opens and a field to add their own custom affirmation. Let the user pick affirmation categories or themes (confidence, calm, focus, morning motivation) that shape what appears. The Saved tab is a collection of favorited and custom affirmations, browsable and shareable. Settings covers daily reminder notifications at chosen times, category selection, name, and appearance. Store the name, favorites, custom affirmations, streak, and notification preferences on-device with no account or server, and schedule local notifications for daily affirmation reminders. Visual style: dark, uplifting aesthetic with rich gradient accents, frosted glass cards, oversized Space Grotesk affirmation type, Inter body, and smooth swipe/spring animations. Offer a free trial, then a one-time paywall unlocking all categories, unlimited saves, custom affirmations, and reminders for a single $2.99 non-consumable in-app purchase ('Unlock lifetime access') via StoreKit 2, with restore purchases.

apps.name: VAULT
apps.oneLiner: Private, locked notes that stay on your device
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that is a private, secure notes app called VAULT where everything stays on-device. Build these screens: a first-run Setup screen to create a PIN with an optional hint, and enable Face ID/Touch ID; a Lock screen requiring the PIN or biometrics to enter; a Notes list screen with search, tag filters, and All/tags organization; an Editor screen to write a note with title and body plus tag assignment; and a Settings screen. Notes auto-lock when the app is backgrounded and reopen only after authentication. Settings covers biometric unlock, changing the PIN, managing tags, appearance, and data. Store all notes, tags, and the PIN securely on-device — encrypt note contents and keep the PIN in the Keychain — with no account, no server, and no cloud sync. Visual style: dark, private aesthetic, frosted glass cards, monospace/Space Grotesk accents for the VAULT wordmark, Inter body, minimal and calm. The free tier allows a limited number of notes; a one-time paywall unlocks unlimited notes and full VAULT Pro for a single $4.99 non-consumable in-app purchase via StoreKit 2 — 'one small payment, unlimited privacy' — with restore purchases.

apps.name: TYMPAN
apps.oneLiner: Real-time environmental EQ for your hearing aids
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that acts as a real-time environmental equalizer for OTC and prescription hearing-aid wearers, retuning their aids to the room they're in rather than to a fixed audiogram. Use the iPhone microphone with an on-device Core ML sound-scene classifier that identifies 30+ environments (restaurant, car cabin, church, kitchen, windy outdoors, quiet home, music) on a rolling 4-second window, and push updated 8-band EQ curves (250Hz–8kHz) to paired aids over Bluetooth LE Audio / MFi with sub-50ms smoothing to avoid pumping. Build four tab-bar screens: Tune (live scene detection with a big animated EQ curve, current room name, and quick 'too quiet / too sharp / I like this' thumbs that train a per-room preference model); History (a listening report with total exposure hours, time-per-environment breakdown, and a loudness safety meter); Presets (custom EQ overrides the wearer can save per room); and Settings. Include a warm, senior-friendly onboarding flow: why we listen, what aids you wear, a room-measurement calibration step, and a live 'TYMPAN is listening' confirmation. Store audiograms, per-room learned curves, and audit logs on-device with optional encrypted iCloud sync to share with an audiologist. Use large legible type, high-contrast accessible colors, generous tap targets, and reassuring medical-calm visuals. Keep all audio processing on-device; never upload raw audio.

apps.name: HERD
apps.oneLiner: Walk the pasture, your phone flags sick livestock
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app for smallholder livestock farmers that turns the iPhone camera into a herd health scanner, flagging lameness, mastitis, early calving, poor body condition, and low rumination before losses compound. Build a Walk mode that uses the camera and on-device Core ML vision (gait keypoints, udder and limb segmentation, body-condition scoring, calving-posture detection) in a walk-by capture at a few frames per second, plus a 60-second microphone rumination check that estimates cud-chews per minute. Identify individual animals by ear-tag OCR or muzzle-print biometrics. Use four bottom tabs: Today (a welcome summary with color-and-icon Alerts and Recent activity), Herd (per-animal profiles with photos and observations), Walk (the live scan), and More (farm name, import/export records, language, clear data). Design voice-first and low-literacy-friendly: every alert plays a short spoken audio clip in the user's language, severity is shown as color plus shape plus icon never text-alone, and iconography leads over words. Support Hindi, Kiswahili, Bengali, Portuguese, and English at launch. Make it fully offline-first: the model and last 30 days of herd data live on-device, syncing to a co-op cloud whenever any connection appears. Store all animal records, photos, and observation logs locally. Tone: respectful of expert farmers, firm and practical, built for women who manage most small-scale dairy.

apps.name: AXLE
apps.oneLiner: Fleet-grade truck safety at a single-truck price
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that gives solo owner-operator truckers fleet-grade safety and compliance from their own phone, mounted on the dash. Use the front camera with on-device Core ML face-landmark and eye-aspect-ratio models for fatigue and micro-sleep detection, head-pose drowsiness alerts, and ergonomic posture coaching with gentle spoken prompts ('lumbar slumped, adjust your seat'). Support English, Spanish, Portuguese, Hindi, Indonesian, and Arabic. Make it offline-first: alerts, logs, and events cache locally on unreliable rural routes and sync when signal returns; store HOS records, trip history, and driver settings on-device. Include an opt-in usage-based-insurance data share for discounts. Visual style is blue-collar and blunt, not Silicon Valley: dark high-contrast dash-readable UI, big numbers, dollars-and-cents pricing, plain language ('your truck' not 'your fleet endpoint'), and messaging that this is for the driver, not the dispatcher. Loud audible fatigue alarms that work with the phone in a windshield mount.

apps.name: DOCKET
apps.oneLiner: Litigation copilot for people without a lawyer
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that helps unrepresented pro-se litigants respond to court cases (eviction, small claims, debt collection, family) before they default. Let the user photograph or scan their court papers with the camera; use Vision text recognition plus an AI layer to read the documents, extract every deadline, and identify the case type and jurisdiction. Show a Your Deadlines home screen with a countdown timeline of critical filing dates and push-notification reminders so nobody misses an answer window. Generate a jurisdiction-correct response and present it across four tabs: Drafted Answer (an editable response document with verified legal citations), Next Steps (a plain-language checklist of what to do and by when), Possible Defenses (relevant defenses for their situation), and Where to File (the correct court, address, and e-filing path). Store scanned papers, extracted deadlines, and drafts on-device; keep sensitive case data private and offline by default. Use a calm, trustworthy, accessible design with clear typography, a reassuring tone, and prominent 'This is decision support, not legal advice' disclaimers on every screen. Prioritize clarity and urgency around deadlines above all else, because most people lose by not answering in time.

apps.name: LULL
apps.oneLiner: Why your baby is crying, in your language

On the home screen show a large 'Tap to listen' button that records the cry with the microphone and runs an on-device Core ML classifier to label it as Hungry, Tired, Pain, Overstimulated, or Colic, with a confidence read and an 'or try a sample cry' option. After classification, launch a warm conversational voice-agent coach that speaks reassuring, dialect-aware guidance scripted by pediatric advisors, respecting the parent's own norms (co-sleeping, baby-wearing) rather than imposing Western cry-it-out methods. Make it offline-first and privacy-first: cry classification runs entirely on-device with no audio uploaded, and coaching transcripts cache locally and sync only when online — because the value is undeniable at 3am with no signal. Store cry logs, sleep data, and baby profile on-device. Design should feel calm, soft, and nighttime-friendly with a dark gentle palette, big touch targets for one-handed exhausted use, and warm encouraging tone. Include an optional paid pediatrician-on-call consult.

apps.name: PLUMB

As the contractor walks a job site, use the camera with live ARKit overlays plus LiDAR (RoomPlan) to measure plumb, level, squareness, and dimensions, and run an on-device Core ML vision model that auto-detects common defects — off-plumb walls, missing trim, paint scuffs, drywall flaws, fixture and cover-plate issues, code violations. Use a rugged high-contrast dark UI readable in bright sun and dusty conditions, big buttons for gloved hands, dollars-and-cents estimates, and plain trade language. Tone is money-forward: this walkthrough just became a paid change-order in ten minutes.

apps.name: RACK

On the Pile screen let the user drop or shoot photos of a heap of clothes; use the camera and multimodal AI vision to segment individual items, grade condition (pilling, hem wear, stains), identify brand, size, and style, and pull real-time sold-comp pricing across Poshmark, Depop, eBay, Vinted, Mercari, and Grailed. apps.name: SOLE
apps.oneLiner: A 30-second daily foot check that saves limbs
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that gives diabetic patients a 30-second daily foot check to catch pre-ulcerative changes before the skin breaks. Each day guide the user through a simple photo capture of both feet ('Left foot first,' then right) using the camera with a real-time coach for lighting, distance, and focus, and a scale-reference calibration. Run an on-device Core ML classifier to detect erythema, edema, callus, and warm/cool temperature-differential zones, comparing today's images against the patient's own rolling 30-day baseline — their healthy foot is the control. Show a 'Today's read' result screen with a clear risk status, per-foot heat indicators labeled Warm or Cool, and a plain explanation; any flagged risk routes to the patient's clinician rather than advising the patient directly. Use four bottom tabs: Check In (the daily capture flow), a foot-history timeline, trends, and profile. Reinforce daily adherence with a streak and gentle reminder notifications, since behavior-change is the whole game. Store foot images and readings in HIPAA-appropriate encrypted on-device storage with secure sync to a clinician dashboard and optional EHR write-back. Design should be calm, clinical, and reassuring, with large accessible type and high contrast for older users and those with low vision. Prominent disclaimer on every screen: SOLE is monitoring and decision support, not diagnosis. The promise is simple and motivating: 30 seconds a day, one foot saved.

apps.name: SPOT
apps.oneLiner: Is it a vet visit? Find out in 30 seconds
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that lets anxious pet parents photograph a lump, rash, or hot-spot on their dog or cat and get an instant triage answer. Open with a 'Is it a vet visit?' home screen and a 'Where's the concern?' body-region picker, then guide the user through a camera capture with a real-time photo coach for lighting, distance, and focus so the image is actually usable. Run a multimodal AI dermatology triage classifier that returns the top-three likely conditions with confidence and a clear escalation level: green 'watch 48 hours,' yellow 'schedule a vet,' or red 'go now.' Include a hard-coded emergency override so that signs of bleeding, seizure, or anaphylaxis immediately show 'GO NOW — do not wait for triage' without running the classifier. When escalated, offer a live vet call with audio and video connecting to a licensed tele-vet network for handoff. Store a Pet Profile with species, breed, age, and breed-specific risk factors (like skin-fold dermatitis in brachycephalic breeds), plus a photo history timeline to track changes over time. Keep triage records and images on-device with an audit trail for every call. Design should be friendly, warm, and pet-parent-reassuring with soft rounded cards, clear color-coded urgency, and calming copy. Prominent 'SPOT is triage, not diagnosis' disclaimer on every screen. The whole value: 30 seconds to know whether to relax, book, or rush in.

apps.name: STACK
apps.oneLiner: Names your indoor air pollution source and the fix
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that names the actual source of indoor air pollution in real time and prescribes a specific fix, pairing with a small Bluetooth multi-gas sensor. Onboard with 'Which rooms do you want to track?', 'Do you already own an air monitor?', and a mic-permission step 'Let STACK listen for pollution sources.' Fuse the sensor's chemical channels (PM, VOC, eCO2, true CO2) with on-device acoustic fingerprinting from the iPhone microphone and time-of-day context to classify the culprit — gas-stove combustion, a candle, hidden mold, off-gassing new furniture — rather than just showing an unlabeled PM2.5 spike. Show a live screen per room with current readings (ppb/ppm), a Listening/Idle/Reading state, and the identified source with a confidence percent, plus a plain action prescription ('Open the north window for 12 minutes, run the range hood at high'). Use bottom tabs for Rooms, an air-quality Report (top sources by room and most-recent entries log), Trends, and Setup with a badge for active alerts. Process all audio on-device — no audio ever leaves the phone — and run account-less by default, with optional opt-in cloud sync of the source-identification log only, never raw readings or audio. Handle sensor OTA model updates over BLE. Store room configs and event history on-device. Lead the design with a strong privacy-first, trustworthy identity; clean modern data-viz with clear color-coded severity, an obvious 'Do →' action for every alert, and a calm confident tone. The differentiator: it names the culprit and tells you exactly what to do.

apps.name: HUM
apps.oneLiner: Daily humming practice for vagal coherence
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that guides a short daily humming practice built around coherent breathing and a chosen healing tone. The app has six swipeable screens: a Welcome hero; a Prepare screen where the user picks a session length (60s reset, 90s daily, or 180s deep) and a tone family (432 Hz Verdi, 528 Hz Solfeggio, or 7.83 Hz Schumann); a live Session screen with a large pulsing breath-pacer ring that scales on a 5-in/5-out coherence cycle, a countdown timer, play/pause and stop controls, and an 'I hummed' button to tag humming moments; a Results screen showing seconds, hums, and Hz for the just-finished session; a History screen with a 14-day contribution-style heatmap, current streak, total minutes, and session count plus a recent-session list; and a Settings screen with a voice-cues toggle, default-frequency picker, and reset-all. Use the iOS AVAudioEngine or a tone generator to synthesize a pure sine tone at the selected frequency with a gentle fade-in/out, and optionally spoken inhale/exhale cues. All sessions, streaks, and preferences persist locally on-device with no account and no network. Visual style: deep near-black background (#0a0a0e), violet accent (#9b6bff), elegant italic Cormorant Garamond serif headlines paired with Inter and a JetBrains-Mono label style, soft radial glow behind the hero, and haptic feedback on tone start and hum tap. Support offline use, a calm reduced-motion option, and Add-to-Home-Screen-quality polish.

apps.name: RHYTHMIX LIVE

apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that turns a musician's finished song into beat-synced AI music videos in multiple aspect ratios. The app has six swipeable screens: a Welcome hero; an Upload & Pipeline screen where the user picks an audio file (WAV/MP3/FLAC/M4A up to ~12 min) via the native file/document picker, then selects one or more AI video engines (Kling, Hunyuan, Luma, MiniMax) and one mood (cinematic, dreamy, hyper, soulful, abstract) as chips; a Beat-Sync viewer that displays an animated waveform with detected BPM (e.g. 120 BPM, 4/4), downbeat shot-cut markers, a moving playhead, and play/reset controls, with bars pulsing near the playhead; a Render Queue screen that renders three deliverables from the same beat grid — 9:16 vertical 60s (TikTok/Reels), 1:1 square 15s (IG grid), and 16:9 landscape 4-min (YouTube) — each with an animated progress bar and status; a History screen with day-streak, total renders, and engines-used stats plus a list of past jobs; and a Settings screen with subscription tiers (Free/Pro $19/Studio $49), a fan-out merch-link toggle, and reset. Detect tempo on-device and store all jobs, selections, and tier locally with no account required; show an offline banner when disconnected. Visual style: near-black purple background (#08050d), hot-pink (#ff1f5a) and cyan (#8af6ff) accents, bold Space Grotesk display type with JetBrains Mono labels, neon glows, and tactile haptics. Native, offline-tolerant, home-screen polished.

apps.name: RESONATE
apps.oneLiner: Generative music that breathes with your body
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that plays a closed-loop generative drone that adapts in real time to the user's heart rate and breathing to pull them toward physiological coherence. The app has six swipeable screens: a Welcome hero; a state-select screen offering three modes — Focus (432·528·648 Hz), Calm (174·396·528 Hz), and Rest (110·220·330 Hz); a live Session player showing live heart-rate (bpm) and breath-rate cards, a breathing gold orb whose radius expands and contracts with the breath, a large coherence score (0–100), a mode pill, and play/cycle-mode/reset controls; a Coherence chart screen with a rolling 30-second sparkline plus peak, average, and current stats; a History screen with streak, session count, and total minutes plus a session list showing mode, duration, and peak/avg coherence; and a Settings screen. Synthesize the drone with three layered oscillators tuned to the mode's frequencies, each with a slow amplitude LFO for shimmer, and detune them tighter as coherence rises — use AVAudioEngine so audio keeps playing and gently retunes when the mode changes. Read biometrics natively: pull heart rate from a paired Apple Watch / HealthKit or Bluetooth HRV strap when available, otherwise fall back to a realistic simulated signal; derive breath from an on-screen pacer. Store all sessions and the selected mode on-device, no account, offline-capable. Visual style: deep navy (#0A0F1F) background, gold (#D4AF37) and cream accents, italic Cormorant Garamond headlines, JetBrains-Mono readouts, a softly pulsing radial-gradient orb, and haptics on session start.

apps.name: Roomtone
apps.oneLiner: Real-time environmental EQ for your hearing aids
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that acts as a real-time environmental equalizer for hearing-aid and headphone users: it listens to the room through the microphone, classifies the acoustic scene, and re-tunes the audio it routes to the user's output on the fly. The main screen is a large scene card that names the currently detected environment (Quiet, Restaurant, Car, Music, Outdoors, or Reverberant) with a live 16-band level meter and a big Start/Stop button. Below it, a scene-chip grid lets the user override auto-detection or return to Auto, and a hold-to-compare button momentarily bypasses processing to A/B the raw room. A Personalize panel holds an 8-band audiogram editor (250 Hz–8 kHz vertical sliders) with mild/moderate hearing-loss presets, plus per-scene EQ fine-tuning that the app remembers and re-applies whenever that scene is detected. Build the audio engine natively with AVAudioEngine: capture mono mic input with echo-cancellation and auto-gain disabled, run a chain of peaking biquad EQ bands (audiogram + scene) into a limiter and master gain, and classify the scene from live spectral features (centroid, band ratios, zero-crossing rate, spectral flatness, RMS) with temporal smoothing. Show a prominent warning to use headphones or paired hearing aids to avoid feedback, and detect mic-permission and no-mic errors gracefully. All processing stays on-device; audiogram and scene tweaks persist locally, works fully offline. Visual style: dark slate (#0d1117) with warm amber (#f4a942) accents, SF-style system typography, large accessible tap targets, high-contrast mode, and clear toasts.

apps.name: READOUT
apps.oneLiner: Scan any page, hear any book aloud

Flow: an animated splash; a three-slide onboarding; a reading-mode picker with four full themes — Standard (dark, elegant), Vision Mode (max-contrast, huge controls, auto-play on text found), Dyslexia (warm background, dyslexia-friendly font, reading ruler), and Elder Mode (extra-large text, simple controls); an optional API-key setup screen (Claude key for OCR/chat, optional ElevenLabs key + voice ID) with a no-key demo; a Library home showing saved books as cards with pages-read, words-heard, and minutes-saved stats; a camera Scanner with a guide frame, animated scan line, capture button, and photo-upload fallback; a processing screen; and a Reader that displays extracted text and highlights each word as it's spoken, with play/pause/skip, adjustable speed, voice selection, live text-size control, bookmarks, a tricky-word syllable helper, and an 'Ask AI' chat sheet to explain any passage. Use the native camera and, where possible, on-device Vision OCR (VNRecognizeText) plus AVSpeechSynthesizer for text-to-speech, with voice commands via speech recognition. Store the library, progress, bookmarks, and keys on-device; keys never leave the phone; works offline for reading saved text. Visual style: deep navy (#030510) with gold (#D4AF37) and purple aurora orbs, Cormorant Garamond and Atkinson Hyperlegible fonts, glassmorphic panels, and generous accessible controls.

apps.name: DREAMS
apps.oneLiner: A generative bedtime ritual and dream journal
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that runs a short nightly bedtime ritual — set an intention, breathe with a guided orb, drift off to a generative soundscape, then capture a moment of morning dream recall. The app has six swipeable screens: a Welcome hero; an Intention screen with a serif text field plus quick chips (Let go, Lucid, Recall, Rest, Safe) that the soundscape composes around; a Ritual player with a large breathing orb that expands and contracts through a 4-7-8 breath cycle (inhale 4, hold 7, exhale 8) for six cycles (~one minute), showing the current phase, a per-second countdown, cycle progress, and play/pause, soundscape-toggle, and reset controls; a Morning Recall screen with a serif journal textarea and mood tags (lucid, vivid, flying, chase, peaceful, fragment); a History/Journal screen with streak, session, and dream-recall counts plus a merged timeline of past rituals and dream entries; and a Settings screen with soundscape-on-by-default and voice-guided-breath toggles, a 432 Hz base note, and reset-all. Generate the soundscape natively with AVAudioEngine as a layered 432 Hz drone (sub-octave 216 Hz + perfect fifth 648 Hz) modulated by slow amplitude LFOs, and optionally speak the breath cues. Store intentions, sessions, and the dream journal on-device with no account, fully offline. Visual style: deep indigo-black (#0B0820) background, violet (#9b6bff) and lavender accents, italic Cormorant Garamond headlines with Inter and mono labels, a soft glowing radial orb, gentle haptics on each breath phase, and a calm reduced-motion option for nighttime use.

apps.name: HerdCheck
apps.oneLiner: Phone-camera livestock screening that works offline
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that lets smallholder dairy and small-ruminant farmers screen animals for lameness, mastitis, and imminent calving using the phone camera, fully offline. The home screen is a Herd list showing registered animals with a health summary; an Add Animal form captures ear-tag/ID, name, species (cow 283-day, buffalo 310-day, sheep 147-day, goat 150-day gestation), birth year, and last-bred date. Each animal opens a Check menu with four options. Lameness: record a walking video with the rear camera and assign a Sprecher 5-point locomotion score (1 normal to 5 severe) with guidance on back-arch and head-bob. Mastitis: photograph the udder from behind — the app analyzes the image for left-vs-right asymmetry and redness, then the user checks visible signs (swelling, asymmetry, redness, heat, pain, yield drop) and milk appearance (normal/watery/clots/blood). Calving predictor: combine gestation day with observed 24-hour signs (vulva swelling, mucus, udder bagging, restlessness, tail position, relaxed pelvic ligaments, off feed, water bag) and an optional photo. Each check produces a color-coded risk tier and recommendation using validated scoring, saved to that animal's history. Include an Alerts dashboard with a badge for high-risk animals, and Settings for farm name, co-op ID, six-language localization (English, Hindi, Bengali, Swahili, Portuguese, Spanish), and CSV/JSON export and share. Use the native camera for photo and video capture and run all image analysis and storage on-device with no account — it is decision support, not a vet replacement. Visual style: earthy dark green (#1a3a2a) with clean cards, large tap targets, bottom tab bar (Herd/Alerts/Settings), and an offline-first PWA-quality feel.

apps.name: Reset
apps.oneLiner: Recovery tracking for team-sport athletes
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that helps team-sport athletes track and improve their recovery between training and games, in a clean iOS-native style. Build a daily recovery check-in where the athlete logs sleep quality and hours, muscle soreness, fatigue, mood, stress, and hydration, and the app computes a single daily readiness/recovery score with a clear color-coded status (ready, caution, rest). Include a Home dashboard showing today's score, a rolling trend chart of recovery over the past week and month, and a streak of consecutive check-ins. Add a guided recovery-tools section — mobility routines, breathing/downregulation sessions, and cooldown timers — plus a history log of past days that the athlete can scroll and review. Let athletes set training/game days so the app flags when readiness is low before a hard session and suggests active recovery. Where possible, pull sleep, resting heart rate, and HRV natively from Apple HealthKit / a paired Apple Watch to auto-fill inputs, otherwise let the athlete enter them manually. Send optional local notifications reminding them to check in each morning. Store all check-ins, scores, and settings on-device with no account and full offline support; the app is a wellness aid, not a medical device. Visual style: polished iOS look with rounded cards, large legible numerals for the recovery score, smooth ring/gauge visualizations, subtle haptics on logging, dark and light appearance support, and generous spacing — a full-screen standalone app experience suitable for adding to the home screen.

apps.name: Codex of Reality
apps.oneLiner: Camera-based HRV coherence with ancient breath protocols
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that is a biofeedback and breathwork platform combining live heart-rate-variability coherence training with guided ancient breathing protocols. The centerpiece is a Coherence Engine: using the rear camera and flash as a photoplethysmography sensor, the user covers the lens with a fingertip and the app reads their pulse from the red-channel signal, detects beats, and computes heart rate, RR interval, RMSSD, and a live 0–100 coherence score measuring how well their heart rhythm syncs with a 5-in/5-out breath pacer. Show a breathing orb that scales with the inhale/exhale phase and shifts from gold to cyan as coherence rises, a beat pulse on each detected heartbeat, and a live readout panel. Include a protocol library organized in four categories — Release (Trauma Shake, Vagus Reset, Fascia Bow), Manifest (Tesla 3-6-9 Breath, Tortoise Breath, Alpha State), Reverse, and Recover (Monk Ritual, Root Lock) — each pairing guided narration with a breath pacer and coherence score. Support optional hardware pairing for sharper data via Bluetooth HRV straps (Polar H10/Verity), Apple Watch/HealthKit, and WHOOP, always keeping the phone camera as a no-hardware default. Run all pulse processing and scoring entirely on-device — nothing uploaded, nothing stored remotely — with local session history offline. Clearly state it is a practice instrument, not a medical device. Visual style: deep midnight-navy (#0a1628) with gold (#d4a843) and coherence-cyan (#5ce5e0) accents, italic Cormorant Garamond display type, JetBrains-Mono readouts, parchment-grain texture, and a breathing sacred-geometry 3-6-9 orb.

apps.name: Buddy System
apps.oneLiner: An ecosystem of caring AI companion personalities
apps.blinkPrompt: Create an iOS app that is an ecosystem of many specialized AI companion personalities the user can talk to for support across mental health, wellness, recovery, career, learning, and identity. The home Hub is a glassmorphic card grid of companions — for example Anxiety Relief, Depression Buddy, Sleep Buddy, Grief, Recovery, ADHD, Study Buddy, Fitness Coach, Financial Coach, LGBTQ+ Ally, and Imposter Syndrome — each with its own emoji/avatar, color glow, and distinct personality. Tapping a companion opens a detail view with tabs: Home (a daily affirmation with read-aloud and refresh, plus a mood check-in — Good/Okay/Struggling — and quick breathing and meditation actions); Chat (a supportive conversation powered by an AI model using that companion's system prompt, with typing indicators); Health (log heart rate, mood, breaths, and sleep, view a 7-day mood trend, and measure heart rate by covering the rear camera and flash for ~20 seconds via on-device PPG); Photos (a memory grid using the native photo picker); Notes (a private journal); and Settings (API keys stored on-device, voice speed, and country). Include automatic crisis-keyword detection that surfaces region-specific hotlines (US/UK/AU) and emergency actions, and native text-to-speech so companions speak, with optional generated portrait/talking-head avatars. Store all chats, moods, health logs, notes, photos, and keys locally on-device; keys never leave the phone. Visual style: deep space-blue (#060912) background with a drifting gradient-mesh, 2026 frosted-glass cards, per-companion colored blooms, Inter/Lexend typography, spring animations, and swipeable screens. It is peer-style support, not a substitute for professional care.
